monuments.name: Agra Fort
monuments.description: The Agra Fort is a historical Mughal fort in the city of Agra, also known as Agra's Red Fort. Mughal emperor Humayun was crowned at this fort in 1530. It was later renovated by the Mughal emperor Akbar from 1565 and the present-day structure was completed in 1573.

monuments.name: Agrasen Ki Baoli
monuments.description: A 60-meter long, 15-meter wide historical stepwell in the heart of Delhi.

monuments.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
monuments.description: A prominent Sikh gurdwara associated with Guru Har Krishan, known for its sarovar and langar.

monuments.name: Humayun's Tomb
monuments.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the earliest examples of Mughal garden-tomb architecture.

monuments.name: India Gate
monuments.description: A war memorial for Indian soldiers who died in World War I and the Afghan Wars.

monuments.name: Isa Khan Niyazi's Tomb
monuments.description: An octagonal tomb of Afghan noble Isa Khan Niyazi, built during his lifetime.

monuments.name: Itmad-Ud-Daula's Tomb
monuments.description: Often called the Baby Taj, this is the tomb of Mirza Ghiyas Beg, built in white marble.

monuments.name: Jama Masjid
monuments.description: One of the largest mosques in India, built by Shah Jahan with red sandstone and white marble.

monuments.name: Jantar Mantar
monuments.description: An astronomical observatory built by Maharaja Jai Singh II to measure time and celestial movements.

monuments.name: Lotus Temple
monuments.description: A Baháʼí House of Worship known for its lotus-like shape and serene ambiance.

monuments.name: Mutiny Memorial (Ajitgarh)
monuments.description: Built to commemorate the British soldiers who died during the 1857 uprising.

monuments.name: Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque
monuments.description: A pre-Mughal mosque inside Purana Qila, combining Lodi and Mughal styles.

monuments.name: Qutub Minar
monuments.description: The tallest brick minaret in the world, built to celebrate Muslim dominance in Delhi.

monuments.name: Quwwat ul-Islam Mosque
monuments.description: The first mosque built in Delhi after the Islamic conquest, located next to Qutub Minar.

monuments.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
monuments.description: The official residence of the President of India, formerly the Viceroy's House during British rule.

monuments.name: Red Fort
monuments.description: A 17th-century Mughal fortress of red sandstone, used as a royal residence and military base.

monuments.name: Taj Mahal
monuments.description: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the right bank of the river Yamuna in Agra, India. It was commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
